reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify domain-relevant, high-impact features based on known socioeconomic patterns, with external XAI tools to provide quantitative, model-learned attributions that capture subtle or non-intuitive feature contributions in the prediction contrast. This ensures both domain knowledge and model-level insight are leveraged effectively.

autonomous_tasks.query: Based on domain knowledge of income prediction in the adult dataset, which features are commonly associated with higher income (>50K) versus lower income (<=50K)?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of key features (e.g., education-num, hours-per-week, occupation) known to correlate with >50K income in the dataset

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the input features in the top-1 (>50K) and top-2 (<=50K) predictions. Identify which features differ in value or category, and assess whether any feature values are consistently higher or more favorable in the >50K class.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A table or list of features with their values and which prediction class they belong to

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP is ideal for contrastive analysis as it provides consistent, interpretable feature attributions across classes using game-theoretic values. LIME helps interpret the top-1 prediction locally by generating a simplified model explaining why the prediction leans toward >50K. Integrated Gradients offer smooth, gradient-based attributions that reveal how the model transitions from baseline to prediction. Sensitivity analysis quantifies the impact of each feature by ablation, directly showing how removing a feature affects class probability, thus identifying critical differentiators.
